outputs.L3:
The video display device includes a liquid crystal display panel that is illuminated from the rear by a plurality of light source substrates. These light source substrates are arranged behind the liquid crystal display panel and function as a backlight for the display.

Each light source substrate is provided with a signal input connector for receiving a control signal. The control signal is used to control the operation of the light source substrate and, in particular, the light emission of the LEDs mounted on that substrate.

Each light source substrate includes a plurality of LEDs. The LEDs correspond to different areas of the liquid crystal display panel, so that the brightness of the backlight can be adjusted on an area-by-area basis. In this way, the display device can control the amount of light supplied to individual regions of the liquid crystal display panel according to the image being displayed.

A driver element is provided to control each LED. The driver element adjusts the luminance of each LED so that the light emitted by the LED corresponds to the brightness of the associated image area on the liquid crystal display panel. As a result, bright image areas can be illuminated with higher luminance, while darker image areas can be illuminated with lower luminance, thereby improving contrast and reducing unnecessary power consumption.

The control signal is transmitted between the light source substrates by connecting a signal output connector of one light source substrate to a signal input connector of another light source substrate. Through this connection structure, the control signal can be sequentially passed from one light source substrate to another, allowing multiple light source substrates to be controlled using a linked signal transmission arrangement.
outputs.L4:
A video display device includes a liquid crystal display panel and a backlight unit disposed on the rear side of the liquid crystal display panel. The backlight unit is divided into a plurality of lighting regions, and a plurality of light source substrates are provided so as to correspond to respective regions of the liquid crystal display panel. Each light source substrate includes a plurality of light emitting elements, such as LEDs, for illuminating a corresponding area of the liquid crystal display panel from the rear.

Each light source substrate is configured to receive a control signal for controlling the light emitting elements mounted on that substrate. The control signal may include luminance control information, image brightness information, timing information, address information, or other data used to determine the amount of light emitted by the LEDs in each region. Based on the received control signal, each light source substrate drives its LEDs so that the luminance of the corresponding backlight area is adjusted according to the brightness or gradation level of the image displayed in the corresponding area of the liquid crystal display panel.

To enable efficient distribution of the control signal, each light source substrate is provided with an input connector and an output connector. The input connector receives the control signal from a control circuit, a preceding light source substrate, or another signal source. The output connector transmits the control signal to a subsequent light source substrate. By electrically connecting the output connector of one light source substrate to the input connector of another light source substrate, the plurality of light source substrates can be connected in series or in a chained configuration.

With this configuration, a single control signal line or reduced number of wiring paths can be used to control multiple light source substrates. The control signal is sequentially supplied from one substrate to the next, allowing each substrate to perform localized backlight control for its corresponding display area. This reduces wiring complexity, improves assembly efficiency, and facilitates modular arrangement of the light source substrates.

The video display device can therefore perform area-specific luminance adjustment, also referred to as local dimming. In darker image regions, the LEDs corresponding to those regions can be driven at a lower brightness or turned off, while in brighter image regions, the corresponding LEDs can be driven at a higher brightness. As a result, the display device can improve contrast, reduce power consumption, suppress unnecessary light leakage, and enhance overall image quality.

Thus, by providing each rear light source substrate with connectors for receiving and forwarding control signals, and by electrically connecting the output connector of one substrate to the input connector of another, the display device enables chained control of localized backlighting. This structure supports flexible arrangement of multiple light source substrates and allows precise luminance control for different areas of the liquid crystal display panel.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a video display device with an LCD panel and multiple daisy-chained LED backlight substrates, each having input/output connectors and local dimming drivers.
counterfactuals.output: A video display device includes a liquid crystal display panel and a backlight assembly disposed behind the liquid crystal display panel. The backlight assembly includes a plurality of LED backlight substrates arranged relative to the liquid crystal display panel and connected in a daisy-chain configuration. Each LED backlight substrate includes a plurality of light-emitting diodes, an input connector configured to receive power and control signals, an output connector configured to transmit the power and control signals to a subsequent LED backlight substrate, and a local dimming driver configured to independently control luminance of one or more corresponding LED groups on the LED backlight substrate. The daisy-chain arrangement reduces wiring complexity between the LED backlight substrates and a controller while enabling zone-based luminance control for local dimming of the backlight assembly in accordance with image data displayed on the liquid crystal display panel.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description of an LCD video display device where each backlight substrate includes LEDs assigned to different screen regions, a driver IC, a signal input connector, and a through-output connector connected to another substrate.
counterfactuals.output:
An LCD video display device includes a liquid crystal display panel and a backlight unit arranged behind the liquid crystal display panel. The backlight unit is divided into a plurality of backlight substrates, each corresponding to one or more predetermined screen regions of the display panel.

Each backlight substrate includes a plurality of light-emitting diodes arranged to illuminate respective assigned regions of the screen. The LEDs may be grouped into independently controllable lighting blocks so that luminance can be adjusted on a region-by-region basis in accordance with a video signal, enabling local dimming or region-specific brightness control.

A driver integrated circuit is mounted on each backlight substrate. The driver IC controls current supplied to the LEDs on the corresponding substrate based on control data received from a display control circuit. The driver IC may include current regulation circuits, dimming control circuits, address decoding circuitry, and communication interface circuitry for receiving brightness commands associated with the screen regions assigned to that substrate.

Each backlight substrate further includes a signal input connector configured to receive power, control signals, clock signals, data signals, or synchronization signals from a preceding circuit or substrate. The signal input connector is electrically coupled to the driver IC and to power distribution wiring formed on the substrate.

In addition, each backlight substrate includes a through-output connector. The through-output connector is electrically connected to the signal input connector and/or to the driver IC through wiring on the substrate, and is configured to output at least a portion of the received signals to another backlight substrate. Accordingly, multiple backlight substrates can be connected in a daisy-chain or cascade configuration, reducing the number of direct connections required between the main control board and the individual backlight substrates.

In operation, a video processing circuit determines luminance information for different screen regions of the LCD panel and transmits corresponding backlight control data to the backlight unit. The data is supplied to a first backlight substrate through its signal input connector. The driver IC on that substrate controls the LEDs assigned to its screen regions, while the through-output connector forwards signals to a subsequent backlight substrate. The subsequent substrate similarly receives the signals through its own signal input connector, drives its assigned LEDs using its driver IC, and may further pass signals to another substrate through its through-output connector.

This configuration allows a large-area LCD video display to be constructed from multiple backlight substrates while maintaining distributed LED drive control. The use of input and through-output connectors simplifies wiring, supports modular assembly, and permits coordinated control of LEDs corresponding to different regions of the screen.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
